Nº 10 · WHY ZODIACS MATTER
AN ESSAY · ABOUT 4 MINUTES

Zodiacs.org runs Astrofolio and wrote this essay. We hold some of these coins and take no fee when you buy one. They are thinly traded and can fall to zero. Full disclosures

B
efore you had a username, you had a sign. Somebody told you when you were small, and you have known it ever since, whether or not you ever read a horoscope. YouGov once showed Americans the twelve signs and asked them to pick their own. Nine in ten could, although only about one in four said they believe in astrology. Very few ideas are known by nearly everyone and owned by no one, and this one has held that position for about 2,400 years.

Almost everyone knows their sign. Few say they believe.

Each grid is one hundred U.S. adults, and each dot one of them. The survey reports each share on its own, not how they overlap, so the two groups are drawn apart.

YouGov, U.S. adults, April 2022. Respondents were shown the twelve signs and asked to pick their own.

It got there by moving. The twelve signs took shape in Babylon and travelled on clay tablets, then in manuscripts, then in printed almanacs. In 1930 a London newspaper printed a horoscope for the newborn Princess Margaret, readers asked for more, and the horoscope column was born. The phone put a sign in every pocket, and today the zodiac is some of the most dependable material on social media. Search any app for your sign and you will find posts from the last hour, most of them made by people who were paid nothing to make them.

The twelve-sign vocabulary survived by moving with people. Coins are its newest form.

In July 2024 twelve coins appeared on Solana, one for each sign. They are memecoins. Anyone can buy one, send one to a friend, and check on a public ledger that it is the one we list. We run the registry that lists them.

Most memecoins do not last a day. CoinGecko studied 18.7 million coins launched on Pump.fun between January 2024 and June 2026 and found that 69% of them traded for the last time on the day they were created. Fewer than one in twenty were still trading ninety days later. A memecoin is built on a joke, and a joke is funniest the first time. The coin lasts as long as people keep retelling it, which for most of them is an afternoon.

Most memecoins stop trading the day they are made.

Each grey dot stands for 10,000 of the 18.7 million coins launched on Pump.fun, lit while they still traded. Each coloured dot is one of the twelve zodiac coins.

CoinGecko, updated 23 June 2026. CoinGecko counted trades on Pump.fun only, so a coin that moved to another exchange may have traded for longer. The twelve were made on 5 July 2024; each was checked for a trade in the 30 days before 10 Nov 2026 on the public ledger.

These twelve are in their third year, and we think the reason is their subject. A meme about a dog is about the dog. A meme about Scorpio is about you, and you will still be a Scorpio when the joke of the month has been forgotten. The zodiac also keeps its own calendar. Every month the Sun enters a new sign, everyone born under it has a birthday coming, and the group chat fills up with it again. Nobody has to schedule any of that.

Each sign is looked up most in its own season.

Sagittarius’s article is read 52% more in its own season than in the rest of the year.
